reasons: Lake identity confirms the case as United States v. William Meyer, Eighth Circuit, decided 2021-12-02, docket 20-2958.
Lake citation record selects 19 F.4th 1028 as the official/display citation, matching the page's reporter citation and 2021 year.

defect.evidence_quote: exigent circumstances exist, and the presence of probable cause allows officers to enter and search the home without one.
defect.locator_note: content_page.md frontmatter holding; opinion text section II before subsections A-C.
defect.problem: The holding is materially supportable, but overbroad as phrased because it says the exigency justifies warrantless entry and seizure without expressly preserving the separate probable-cause requirement; it also states the police-created-exigency limit only as threatening unlawful conduct, while the opinion frames it as engaging or threatening to engage in Fourth Amendment violations.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to say that, where officers have probable cause and a sufficient basis to believe evidence will be imminently destroyed, exigent circumstances justify warrantless entry/search unless officers created the exigency by engaging or threatening to engage in Fourth Amendment-violating conduct.

reasons: The opinion supports the knock-and-talk premise and the destruction-of-digital-evidence exigency on these facts.
The opinion separately holds probable cause existed before upholding the warrantless entry/search.
residual_risks: If used as a general rule statement, the current wording could be read to omit probable cause as an independent prerequisite.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the probable-cause requirement and use the opinion's full King formulation: engaging or threatening to engage in conduct violating the Fourth Amendment.

reasons: The opinion directly analyzes a claimed destruction-of-evidence exigency for warrantless home entry.
The related/cross-doctrine role is supported because the case also involves knock-and-talk and police-created-exigency issues.
residual_risks: The opinion concerns destruction of evidence, not hot pursuit specifically, despite the combined home-page title.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Clarify on the home page, if needed, that Meyer is a destruction-of-evidence exigency case rather than a hot-pursuit case.

reasons: The opinion's police-created-exigency analysis expressly addresses the agents' knock-and-talk as a valid investigative technique.
The facts began with agents going to Meyer's home, knocking, and questioning him, so the Knock and Talk home role is supported.
residual_risks: The case is key mainly for the knock-and-talk/police-created-exigency interface, not for every knock-and-talk issue.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Frame the role as key for knock-and-talk leading into claimed police-created exigency.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A's charter.
The content treatment fields match the lake treatment stub: unverified, null dates/basis refs, no point overrides, and frontier-stub scope note.
residual_risks: No Lens A treatment finding made.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A's charter.

residual_risks: No Lens A treatment finding made.
